text: 19h Edited We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe. We’ve been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused. 3,108 404 Comments Like Comment Share Revolut 9h Due to a recent Google Cloud outage, customers may have experienced temporary service disruption on the Revolut app today. The issue has now been fixed, and services are now restored. All our customers’ money and data is safe, and has remained safe throughout this incident. We apologise for any inconvenience caused. Like Reply 13 Reactions Johannes Hamman 17h Probably should have hired me. You know it’s really bad when even your customer support goes down. Which means there’s no redundancy and they have shared infrastructure for all systems. Support should run on a decoupled channel and core systems should have failover redundancy. Losing access via the app is one thing, also not being about to use your card to pay is a major failure of risk management. Wondering if someone vibe coded a bad release or if this was something more sinister…waiting for that explanation, it’s going to be well scrutinised as their architecture should have been. author: Klarna
text: 1d Klarna is now live at 100,000 U.S. in-store locations through Clover, and we’re taking our partnership with Fiserv further. 🚀 Klarna will be available on Commerce Hub, Fiserv’s enterprise commerce platform, for the first time. Enterprise merchants in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and select European markets can offer Klarna in-store and online. Consumers can pay in full, pay in 30 days, or split purchases into interest-free installments. Each option comes with a new credit decision on every transaction. Distribution partnerships like this are central to how we grow our network. They put clear, flexible ways to pay in front of consumers wherever they shop.
